hypothesis: The five tee-modified straight FRAME sources are ordinary flexible pipe beneath independently owned B31J end-condition flexibility. Because the solver builds the base frame and gravity/initial-load vectors first and then condenses the B31J rotational springs and rigid offsets consistently, the accepted common Timoshenko beam law can be tested under the unchanged tee modifier without changing directional B31J factors. The tee-owned bend incoming straight source 36 remains held so bend and tee family changes are not bundled.

decisionReason: Corrected exact-head run 31318659758 completed successfully with unchanged candidate mechanics, preserved tee modifier semantic hashes, 12/12 bend coverage and target equilibrium at numerical roundoff. The tee-FRAME extension is strongly favorable locally: L19 node 20090 FY error falls from 8.542% to 2.104%; all six carried I019 sources-9-11 MZ failures resolve; L19 displacement/rotation failures fall 66 -> 48 and L20 displacement/rotation failures 90 -> 83. However isolated promotion violates the M047 no-new-L19-restraint gate: node 20390 FZ moves from the accepted-I015 9.961% error to 10.808%, creating one L19 restraint failure. L19 source-action count improves 23 -> 17 but aggregate source-action RMSnorm slightly worsens; a new source-44 MZ failure appears on the bend-side I020 boundary. L20 restraint count stays 6 but restraint RMS worsens and source-end-action failures rise 134 -> 166 despite improved source-action RMS. Therefore the common base-beam shear hypothesis beneath B31J remains supported locally, but this five-source tee-only system cutover is not accepted as final architecture. The result reinforces node 20390/source44 as cross-family sentinels and shows special-component boundaries must be resolved coherently before broader promotion.
